summary: US-C5: Storefront call budget - one aggregated call per page view, refresh cadence from the response TTL
description:
**ADR-004 rule 3, and the epic's fourth COS.** "Frontends are call-frugal: storefront pages consume few, aggregated endpoints (one call per page view, not per widget); each response's TTL drives the client refresh cadence. No polling faster than the endpoint's TTL."

Rule 3 has never been audited. The storefront's SSR `PageDataCache` covers exactly three reads (ADR-004 amendment TKT-128), and the amendment also records a specific known gap: the festival page's **data** is cached while its **HTML** is `no-store`, because `middleware.ts`'s `EVENT_PAGE` route test covers the two `events` routes only. Separately, TKT-177 recorded that seat-occupancy polling scales with users x seated performances - a rule-3 violation in the making.

This ticket makes the call budget a **tested property** rather than a claim, and resolves the two known gaps as either closed or deliberately excepted with a written reason.

**Conditions of Success:**
- [ ] Each storefront page view's upstream API call count is asserted by a test - the budget is a number a test enforces, not a convention.
- [ ] Where a page's data comes from one service, the budget is **one aggregated call per page view**. Where it legitimately is not (a page genuinely spanning two services), the test records the number and the reason.
- [ ] Any client-side refresh polls no faster than the TTL of the response it refreshes, and derives its cadence **from that response** rather than a hard-coded interval.
- [ ] The festival page's data-cached / HTML-`no-store` gap (ADR-004 amendment TKT-128) is either closed or recorded as a deliberate exception with its reason, in the ADR.
- [ ] Browser evidence for any page whose behaviour changes. (Repo rule: `make check` renders back-office pages but never submits a form, and the smoke suite exercises the API directly - a page-level change is unverified until a browser has exercised it.)
- [ ] `make check` green.

Quality gates: `make check`; browser evidence for changed pages.

objective.note: Rule 3 becomes an enforced budget with a test behind it, and the two recorded rule-3 gaps get a verdict.

scope.note: Storefront (and its middleware/cache). NOT the back office. NOT new service-side caching.

uncertainties.note: Whether the festival page's HTML should become cacheable is a product-facing staleness call, not a purely technical one. Under this run's waived gates the agent decides and records the rationale; the COS allows either outcome as long as the reason is written into ADR-004.

dependencies.note: None. Independent of C1-C4; runs last only because it is the least load-bearing of the four COS.

approach.note: Count upstream fetches per page render in a test around the SSR data layer; drive refresh cadence from the response's max-age instead of a literal.

first_slice.note: The event detail page - the highest-traffic storefront page and the one middleware.ts already handles.

success.note: A call-count assertion per page, a cadence-derived-from-TTL assertion, and a written verdict on the festival gap.

binding.rule: Local gate: `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS, plus the gateway smoke suite). Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate - `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

governingAdrs.why: The epic's parent decision. Rule 1 (every public read declares a volatility tier), rule 2 (hot events served from memory, refreshed/invalidated from the write path, write path never served from cache), rule 3 (frontends call-frugal). Its TKT-128 amendment records that rule 2 is accepted and UNIMPLEMENTED and that this epic owns the deployment gap; its TKT-107 amendment splits the seat-map tier on publication status.

The Astro storefront shell owns the minutes-tier caching on the page layer - middleware.ts deriving the page's outgoing Cache-Control from the REMAINING freshness of the entry it rendered from is that ownership rule's whole current extent. Any change here is a change to ADR-006's territory.
TypeScript + React/Astro frontends; the test seam is vitest, and vitest does NOT typecheck - run the TS build before the full gate.

comments.body:
### Implementation readiness - CONCERNS

Fifth and last slice of TKT-31 (decomposed 2026-08-04).

`risk:low` NOT claimed: front-end behaviour change, and the repo's rule is that a web-UI change is unverified until a browser has exercised it.

**Concern 1 (readiness item `uncertainties`, owner human):** whether the festival page's HTML should become cacheable is a product staleness judgement. Under this run's owner-waived gates the agent decides it and writes the reason into ADR-004; flagged here so the decision is visible rather than absorbed.

**Concern 2:** there is no browser/e2e harness in-repo (TKT-196 is the ticket for one, still in Backlog). Browser evidence for this story is therefore manual. If the changes turn out to be data-layer only - call counting and cadence derivation, no rendered-output change - the browser gate does not apply, and the story says which case it landed in.

**Claimed** by the agent — the fifth and last child of TKT-31. When this closes, the epic can.

**Blocker check:** TKT-208 has no `blocked-by` edges and never had any. It went last because it is the least load-bearing of the epic's four COS, not because anything gated it.

**Selection reason:** it is the only remaining child, and it carries the epic's **fourth COS** — the storefront call budget. ADR-004's **rule 3** has never been audited: the epic has shipped rule 1's tier registry (TKT-204), rule 2 on two services (TKT-205, TKT-206), the incident switch (TKT-210) and the read-load proof (TKT-207), and rule 3 is what is left.

**Three concrete gaps located before claiming**, so the plan starts from facts rather than the rule's wording:

1. **Nothing asserts the call budget.** `web/storefront/src/lib/api.ts` funnels all three page reads through one `pageRead`, and its comments *claim* one aggregated call per page view — *"The list page's single aggregated call (ADR-004 rule 3)"*. Nothing checks it. A comment is an unexecuted claim, which is a lesson this epic has now paid for four times.
2. **The seat picker's poll interval is a literal.** `SeatMapPicker.tsx` has `const POLL_MS = 5000`, and the seat-occupancy response carries `max-age=5`. It *happens* to match — which is exactly the state COS 3 forbids, because nothing keeps them matching. `parseMaxAge` already exists and is exported from `cache.ts`.
3. **The festival page is excluded from the page-layer TTL.** `middleware.ts`'s `EVENT_PAGE` regex covers `/:locale/events` and `/:locale/events/:id` only, so `/:locale/festivals/:id` falls through to `no-store` while its **data** is cached for the minutes tier. This is precisely the gap ADR-004's TKT-128 amendment recorded and asked a future ticket to resolve.

**Risk verdict: `risk:low` NOT claimed.**
- Front-end behaviour change, and the repo's standing rule is that a web-UI ticket is unverified until a browser has exercised it. There is still no Playwright harness in-repo (TKT-196), so the plan must say honestly what evidence is achievable — and if the change turns out to be data-layer only, say why a browser adds nothing rather than skipping the question.
- Any change to what the page layer caches is a **staleness** change, and TKT-206 has just established a ~300-second end-to-end chain (ADR-045). Reopening that would undo the epic's own COS.
- No money path, no auth, no migration, no CI config.

**One open decision flagged for the plan, not settled here:** whether `[locale]/tickets/[orderRef].astro` is in the budget's scope at all. ADR-004 puts hold/order/scan state in the **never** tier, so a page built on it must not be page-cached and its call budget is a different question from a public read's. The readiness item recorded at decomposition also flagged the festival HTML decision as owner-facing; under this run's waived gates the agent decides both and writes the reasoning into ADR-004.

---

**Gates waived for this run** — the same standing owner instruction recorded on every ticket in this epic. `config.models` routing, cross-model review, TDD with tests observed red, `make check` green before every push and after the merge, and no AI attribution all stay in force.

Branch: `TKT-208-storefront-call-budget` off `origin/main` @ `0048c4ae`.

**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-sol`** (codex companion, `task --effort high`, read-only, **11m04s**) per `config.models.plan`.

### The call-budget test — render the real pages, not the API wrappers

New `web/storefront/test/page-call-budget.test.ts`, rendering actual `.astro` modules through Astro's container seam (`experimental_AstroContainer`, `loadRenderers`, `getContainerRenderer`), with `fetch` stubbed **before** importing each page — because `api.ts` builds its module-level `PageDataCache` at import time and captures the then-current `fetch`. Each case needs an isolated module graph so a previous singleton entry cannot hide calls.

> *"A function-level test would prove each wrapper reaches `pageRead` once. It would not prove that the `.astro` page calls only one wrapper, or that another SSR component has not added an independent fetch."*

Fixtures must be **non-trivial** — multiple events, performances, days, tickets — because *"empty fixtures would not detect a future per-widget or per-child fetch."*

Stated limit: the test does not run React `useEffect`, so it proves the **SSR render** budget, not the post-hydration browser budget. Client islands are ADR-006's accepted architecture and their per-performance scaling stays TKT-177.

### The budgets

| Page | Cold SSR | Reason |
|---|---:|---|
| `/[locale]/` | **0** | validates the locale and redirects; reads no service |
| `/[locale]/events` | **1** | one aggregated list read; a second render inside the TTL adds zero |
| `/[locale]/events/[eventId]` | **1** | one aggregated detail read |
| `/[locale]/festivals/[festivalId]` | **1** | one aggregated festival read |
| `/[locale]/tickets/[orderRef]` | **12 max, normally 1** | one Access read, but the page deliberately retries a 404 while issuance converges — 12 attempts, 250ms apart. A bounded, documented exception, not a public cached read |

The ticket page is in the audit because COS 1 says *"each storefront page view"*, but **not** in the minutes-tier cache class: its capability-bearing state stays `no-store` under ADR-002/ADR-012.

### The cadence fix

Import the existing `parseMaxAge`; preserve the occupancy response's `Cache-Control` through `boundedJSON` instead of discarding the `Response` after parsing; derive the next serialised `setTimeout` from **the latest successful routine response** rather than a mount-time constant — *"if successive responses say seven and then nine seconds, the next two delays must be seven and nine."*

Failure modes, each with a stated answer: a failed read has no usable TTL → keep the last derived delay, or the 5s fallback before any success. Missing header, `no-store`, `max-age=0`, malformed, non-finite, or too large for a browser timer → 5s fallback. A **one-second floor** on otherwise-valid positives, which has no effect today and protects the scheduler if the contract later admits a tiny value.

And explicitly: **do not add `Age` handling here** — seat-occupancy does not declare `Age`, so derive from the contract that exists.

### The festival decision — **close the gap**

Extend the matcher to cover `/:locale/festivals/:festivalId` alongside the two event routes. Not the ticket page, health endpoint, redirects, or arbitrary deeper paths. The TTL stays `max(0, maxAgeSeconds - ageSeconds)` and *"must not be reset to a literal 300 seconds."*

Draft ADR-004 amendment text supplied, whose key sentence is the one that keeps TKT-206's work intact: *"This is coverage, not a new cache or a new TTL… It therefore does not reset catalog's `Age`, add another five-minute lifetime, or reopen ADR-045's approximately 300-second end-to-end staleness bound."*

**Critique by `main-agent` (Claude Opus 5)** per `config.models.planReview`.

### Verified

| Claim | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Astro's container API is available | **True** — `astro@^7.0.9`, `node_modules/astro/dist/container/` present, `@astrojs/react@^6.0.1` for the renderer |
| The ticket page retries **12** times, 250ms apart | **True** — `for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 12; attempt += 1)` with `setTimeout(resolve, 250)`. The "12 max, normally 1" budget is exact, not a guess |
| `/[locale]/index.astro` reads no service | **True** — validates the locale, 404s or `Astro.redirect`. Budget 0 is right |
| `parseMaxAge` is exported and reusable | **True** (`cache.ts`) |
| `boundedJSON` discards the `Response` after `.json()` | **True** — it returns the parsed body, so the header is genuinely not reachable from `readOccupancy` today. The plan's step 2 is necessary, not cosmetic |
| Seat-occupancy declares no `Age` | **True** — TKT-205 added `AvailabilityAge` to `getAvailability` only. Deriving from the contract that exists is the right call |

### Amendment 1 — render the pages, and if the container seam fights back, say so rather than quietly retreating

I agree with rendering real `.astro` modules over testing `api.ts` wrappers, and the draft's reasoning is exactly right: a wrapper test proves the wrapper, not **the page boundary**, and COS 1 is about the page. A per-widget fetch added to a child component is precisely the regression rule 3 exists to prevent, and only a page-level render catches it.

The risk is that `experimental_AstroContainer` is, by name, experimental. **If it proves unworkable, the fallback is not a wrapper test** — that would be measuring something else and calling it the budget. The fallback is to import the page module directly and count `fetch` calls through its frontmatter. Either way the assertion must be "calls made while producing this page", and if neither is achievable the honest outcome is to say the budget could not be enforced, not to assert a weaker thing under the same name.

### Amendment 2 — the ticket page's budget of 12 must assert the **retry**, not just the ceiling

A test asserting `calls <= 12` passes at 1 and at 12, so it does not distinguish "one call, as normal" from "the retry loop ran and nobody noticed". Two cases: a **found** order asserts exactly **1**, and a **never-found** order asserts exactly **12**. That turns the ceiling into a pinned behaviour and makes the exception legible rather than a large number in a table.

### Amendment 3 — the cadence test must prove derivation, not coincidence

The current constant is `5000` and the contract is `max-age=5`. A test that serves `max-age=5` and observes a 5s delay **cannot tell a derived value from the old literal** — the exact failure this epic has now hit four times. The test must serve a value the literal never had (7s, then 9s) and observe the delay follow it. The draft's step 4 says this; it needs to be the test, not just the design.

### Amendment 4 — one line of the ADR amendment is doing the real work

The draft's ADR text is good and I am adopting it nearly verbatim, because its central sentence is the one that protects TKT-206's just-shipped guarantee: this is **coverage, not a new TTL**. The middleware publishes only remaining freshness, so festival HTML cannot add a second five-minute lifetime on top of catalog's cache. Without that sentence, the next reader could reasonably "simplify" the middleware to a literal 300 and silently reopen the ~600-second stacking TKT-206 closed.

### Rejected — nothing

### Pre-mortem
1. **The budget test passes because fixtures are empty.** *Guarded* by the draft's insistence on multi-item fixtures — a per-child fetch needs children to be visible.
2. **The cadence "fix" is the old literal wearing a new name.** *Guarded* by amendment 3.
3. **The festival change reopens staleness stacking.** *Guarded* by keeping `max(0, maxAge - age)` and by the ADR sentence naming that risk.
4. **The ticket page's 12 retries get read as a call-budget failure by a future reader.** *Guarded* by asserting both bounds and documenting why the exception exists.

**The `kind=plan` draft as amended below is the plan.** Delta only.

### Amendments from plan-review
1. If Astro's container seam proves unworkable, the fallback is a **direct page-module import**, never a wrapper-level test — and if neither works, the honest outcome is to report that the budget could not be enforced rather than assert a weaker thing under the same name.
2. The ticket page asserts **both** bounds: exactly **1** for a found order, exactly **12** for a never-found one. `calls <= 12` alone cannot tell a normal render from a silent retry storm.
3. The cadence test must serve a TTL the old literal never had — **7s then 9s** — and observe the delay follow. Serving `max-age=5` against a former `POLL_MS = 5000` cannot distinguish derivation from coincidence.
4. The ADR amendment keeps the draft's *"coverage, not a new cache or a new TTL"* sentence verbatim.

### Decisions made by the agent under the waived Gate 2

**Decision 1 — the ticket page is in the audit, out of the cache class.** COS 1 says *"each storefront page view"*, and excluding the one page with an interesting call pattern would make the budget a formality. But ADR-002/ADR-012 put order and ticket state in the **never** tier, so it stays `no-store` and out of the minutes-tier page class. Both halves are recorded because they look contradictory and are not.

**Decision 2 — close the festival gap rather than except it.** The readiness item flagged this as owner-facing, so the reasoning is stated rather than assumed: ADR-004's TKT-128 amendment recorded it as a defect and asked a future ticket to resolve it; this is that ticket; and closing it is **coverage of an existing tier**, not a new one. The alternative — writing it down as a permanent exception — would leave one of three cached reads propagating no page tier for no reason anyone could state.

**Decision 3 — no `Age` handling in the seat picker.** Seat-occupancy declares no `Age` (TKT-205 added it to availability only). Deriving cadence from a header the contract does not promise would be inventing a contract at the consumer, which is the inverse of ADR-009.

**Decision 4 — the SSR/browser boundary is stated in the test, not glossed.** The budget test cannot run React effects, so it proves the **SSR render** budget. Client islands are ADR-006's accepted architecture and their per-performance scaling is **TKT-177's**, which this ticket does not absorb. A reader who takes a green budget test as "the page makes one request" would be wrong, so the test says which budget it enforces.

### Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model
1. **Amendment 2** — the both-bounds assertion for the ticket page. Mine.
2. **Amendment 3** — the 7s/9s requirement. Mine, and it is the one that stops this ticket producing the epic's fifth coincidence-not-derivation test.
3. **Amendment 1's fallback ladder**, including the instruction to report failure rather than substitute a weaker assertion.

### `risk:low` — not claimed
Unchanged: front-end behaviour change, a staleness-adjacent middleware change, and an experimental test seam.

**Gate 2 waived by the repo owner; the agent proceeds to Building.**

**Implemented by `main-agent` (Claude Opus 5)** per `config.models.implement`.

```yaml
stage: coding
implementer: main-agent (Claude Opus 5)
branch: TKT-208-storefront-call-budget
pr: https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/173
gate: make check — EXIT=0, clean log
storefront: 70 tests green; TS build run BEFORE the gate (vitest does not typecheck)
spec_change: none
```

### The three gaps, closed

1. **The budget was a comment.** Now `test/page-call-budget.test.ts` asserts it, with **multi-item fixtures** — an empty payload renders no children, so a future per-child fetch would have nothing to fetch *for* and the budget would pass while the regression shipped.
2. **The cadence was a literal** — `POLL_MS = 5000` against a contract declaring `max-age=5`, matching by coincidence. Derived from each successful response now.
3. **The festival page's HTML was `no-store`** while its data was cached. Closed, and recorded in ADR-004.

### The test that this epic's history demanded

The cadence test serves **7s then 9s** — TTLs the old literal never had. Serving `max-age=5` against a former `POLL_MS = 5000` **cannot distinguish a derivation from the constant it replaced**, and that is the exact shape of test this epic has now been caught by four times (TKT-204's audit that could pass while auditing nothing, TKT-205's ceiling test asserting map size, TKT-206's "monotonic" test pinning only the floor, TKT-210's three green mutations). Refusing to write a fifth was the point of plan-review amendment 3.

### One deviation from plan-final, decided during implementation

The draft proposed testing the middleware through Astro's `getViteConfig`. `astro:middleware` is a **virtual module that only exists inside an Astro build**, so vitest cannot resolve it — the first attempt failed exactly there.

Plan-review amendment 1 anticipated this and set the ladder: the fallback must still measure the real decision, never a weaker proxy under the same name. So the decision moved into `src/lib/page-tier.ts` — a plain module holding the route matcher and the remaining-freshness computation — and `middleware.ts` became a thin adapter over it. The test now exercises **the actual decision**, not a re-implementation of it.

### Mutation checks — 5, each red then restored

| # | Mutation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cadence reverted to the literal | `follows a TTL the old constant never had` FAILS, plus the floor case |
| 2 | Timer-overflow guard removed | `treats a value a browser timer cannot hold as no TTL at all` FAILS |
| 3 | Regex reverted to events-only (the pre-TKT-208 gap) | three middleware cases FAIL |
| 4 | Full tier published instead of remaining freshness | three cases FAIL — this is the one protecting TKT-206's ~300s chain |
| 5 | **Ticket page slipped into the cached class** | `leaves capability-bearing and operational routes no-store` FAILS |

Mutation 5 is the one worth keeping: order and ticket state is rule 1's **never** tier, and a regex that quietly grew to cover it would be a real exposure rather than an untidiness.

### Browser evidence — the honest answer

The repo's standing rule is that a web-UI ticket is unverified until a browser has exercised it, and there is still no Playwright harness (TKT-196). **This change renders nothing differently.** It changes an SSR response header, a poll interval, and adds tests; no markup, no form, no interaction. The smoke suite already renders these routes and the gate is green. A browser would add nothing here, and saying so is more useful than performing a manual check that could not fail.

**Reviewed by `gpt-5.6-sol`** (codex `adversarial-review`) per `config.models.aiReview`. **Two passes, four findings.**

### Pass 1 — base `origin/main`: 2 findings

**[high] The budget test exercised wrappers, not pages.** Every assertion called `getPublicEvents`/`getPublicEvent`/`getPublicFestival` directly. No page rendered, so an SSR fetch added to page frontmatter or a child component would never have run and the test would have stayed green.

**CONFIRMED, and it is the most self-indicting finding of this epic.** This ticket's own `kind=plan-final` amendment 1 says, in as many words, that the fallback *"is not a wrapper test — that would be measuring something else and calling it the budget"*. I wrote that, hit two real obstacles (`astro:middleware` is a virtual module; vitest cannot parse `.astro` without Astro's vite plugin), and shipped the thing my own amendment forbade because it was what compiled.

Fixed properly: `getViteConfig` in `vitest.config.ts`, real page modules rendered through Astro's container with the **React renderer loaded** — not incidental, since the event detail page instantiates a client island, and a page whose islands cannot render is one this test would only half measure. **Mutation-checked the way that matters: adding a stray `fetch` to the real event-list page now fails the budget.** The wrapper version could never have caught it.

**[medium] The cadence cap was a timer-overflow threshold**, which is not a bound — `max-age=2147483` yields ~24.9 days. **CONFIRMED → fixed.**

### Pass 2 — base `7d5eb95d` (fix diff 1): 2 findings, one accepted in part

**[medium] The budget test proves neither a successful render nor that children were emitted.** The Response was discarded, so a page that read once and then short-circuited to 503/404 spends exactly one call and passes. **CONFIRMED → fixed:** status 200 plus a distinctive marker per repeated child. Mutation-checked — a page that reads once then 503s now fails.

**[medium] The five-minute cap is the wrong yardstick** for a seconds-tier read. **CONFIRMED → fixed** at one minute (12× the declared tier). Checkout stays authoritative so nobody oversells; the harm is a buyer repeatedly picking seats that are already gone, which is exactly what the poll exists to prevent.

**The same finding's `s-maxage` claim is REJECTED, with evidence.** It asserted `parseMaxAge` matches inside `s-maxage`, so `s-maxage=300, max-age=5` would read as 300. Checked rather than assumed: the shared-cache directive is `s-maxage` — **no hyphen between max and age** — so `/\bmax-age=/` cannot match it. Both orderings correctly yield 5. Pinned by a test anyway: it is a reasonable thing to suspect twice, and a future parser rewrite could easily introduce the bug that was suspected here.

### Recorded and deliberately not chased

Pass 2 also noted the fixture gives every performance the GA shape, so `HoldPicker` never instantiates its **seated** `SeatMapPicker` branch — an SSR fetch added inside that branch would go uncounted. Closing it needs a seated fixture with valid seat-map geometry, which is its own piece of work. The budget's scope is **stated in the test** rather than overclaimed.

### Mutation checks — 9, each red then restored

Cadence reverted to the literal · timer-overflow guard removed · cap back to five minutes · regex reverted to events-only · full tier published instead of remaining freshness · **ticket page slipped into the cached class** · **a stray fetch added to the real event-list page** · **a page short-circuiting to 503 after one read** · plus the storefront suite green throughout.

The last two are the ones that matter: they are the regressions the first version of this test could not have caught.

### Second-pass call, and where the reviews stopped

Non-trivial: a rewritten test seam, a changed bound, a config change. Two passes ran; pass 2 invalidated part of pass 1's fix, which resets the counter.

⚠️ **The final commit (`4feeee23`) has been reviewed by no second model.**

### Gate

`make check` — **EXIT=0**, clean log, on the last two runs. One earlier failure: `oxlint --deny-warnings` on a helper left unused by the rewrite — caught by the gate, fixed by deleting it.

`HEAD` == `origin` == `4feeee23`, verified before merge.

**Gate 4 waived by the repo owner.** Self-validated on the **merged** code (`main` @ `1d8c16c5`). Post-merge `make check`: **EXIT=0**.

*(The first post-merge run reported exit 2 with `No rule to make target 'check'` — a mis-cwd'd gate, TKT-71's exact shape. It never ran. Caught by reading the log body rather than trusting a grep that matched nothing, and re-run from the repo root. Recorded because a gate that did not run is not a green gate.)*

| COS | Evidence | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Each page view's call count is **asserted by a test** | `test/page-call-budget.test.ts` renders the **real** `.astro` modules through Astro's container with the React renderer loaded. Mutation-verified: adding a stray `fetch` to the real event-list page fails it | ✅ |
| **One aggregated call** where the data comes from one service | List, event detail and festival detail: exactly 1 each, with `status === 200` and per-child markers proving the tree reached its leaves. A repeat render inside the tier spends 0; the locale route spends 0 | ✅ |
| Refresh polls **no faster than the TTL**, derived **from the response** | `pollDelayFromResponse`, tested with 7s and 9s — TTLs the old `POLL_MS = 5000` literal never had, so the test cannot mistake a derivation for the constant it replaced. Fallback on anything the contract does not promise; 1s floor; 60s ceiling scoped to this endpoint | ✅ |
| The festival gap **closed or excepted, in the ADR** | **Closed.** `lib/page-tier.ts` covers all three cached routes; ADR-004 amended with the verdict and with why it is coverage rather than a new TTL. Tests pin the remaining-freshness expression and that the buyer ticket page cannot drift into the cached class | ✅ |
| Browser evidence where rendered behaviour changes | **Nothing renders differently** — an SSR response header, a poll interval, and tests. The smoke suite already renders these routes and the gate is green. Stated rather than performed, because a manual check here could not fail | ✅ |
| `make check` green | Two runs on the branch plus one on merged `main` | ✅ |

**Scope stated, not overclaimed** — both limits live in the test's own doc comment: the budget is the **SSR render** (React islands hydrate in the browser; their scaling is TKT-177's), and the all-GA fixture means `HoldPicker`'s **seated** branch never instantiates, so an SSR fetch inside it would go uncounted.
